title: Custom providers and the model list — questions before anything is drawn

steps.intro: How someone connects a service that isn't OpenRouter, ChatGPT or Claude.

steps.path: Assistant settings → Cloud providers → Add provider
steps.headline: How should someone connect a service like Inception, Groq or DeepSeek?
steps.today: Add provider offers Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or "Custom endpoint (OpenAI-compatible)". The last one asks for a web address you have to find in the service's documentation.
steps.problem: Most people don't know what an OpenAI-compatible endpoint is or where to find its address, so the services they've heard of look unsupported.
steps.proposal: The app already downloads a public list of about 200 AI services with their addresses. Add provider could search it by name and fill in the address for you.

options.label: Search by name
pros: Type "Inception", pick it, paste your key — done.
Models, prices and context sizes appear straight away.
cons: One more thing on the form.
A service missing from the list still needs the address typed.

options.label: Keep the address field
pros: Nothing new to learn for people who already use it.
cons: You still have to look up the address yourself.
Models only appear if the app recognises the address.

steps.path: Assistant settings → Cloud providers → Add provider
steps.headline: If the key or address doesn't work when you press Add, what should happen?
steps.today: Add provider saves without checking. You only find out it's wrong when a chat fails, or if you press Test on the provider afterwards.
steps.problem: A typo in a key or address shows up later as a confusing chat error, far from where it was made.
steps.proposal: Pressing Add checks the connection right away. The question is what happens when the check fails.

options.label: Save, show the problem
pros: The problem and a way to fix it sit on the provider.
cons: A broken provider exists until you fix or remove it.

options.label: Don't save until it works
cons: A service that is briefly down can't be added at all.
You have to keep the form open while you fix things.

steps.path: Assistant settings → Cloud providers and Local models
steps.headline: Where should a provider on this computer (like Ollama) appear after you add it?
steps.today: You add it on Cloud providers, but because its address is on this computer it silently moves to the Local models page.
steps.problem: It looks like it disappeared the moment you added it.
steps.proposal: Two ways to stop that surprise.

options.label: Move it, say so
pros: A line tells you where it went.
cons: Still on a different page than where you added it.

options.label: Show on both
pros: It's wherever you look for it.
cons: The same provider listed twice is confusing to edit or remove.

steps.intro: What the app does when it can't find out how much a model can read.

steps.path: A provider's Settings, under Cloud providers
steps.headline: When the app can't find a model's context size, where should you set it?
steps.today: If the app can't learn how much text a model can read at once, it quietly assumes 32,000 tokens — even for models that handle a million.
steps.problem: Long chats get shortened far sooner than needed, and nothing tells you why.
steps.proposal: The provider says "Context size unknown" with a way to set it. It could be set once for the whole provider, or per model.

options.label: Once per provider
pros: Fits the common case: one server running one or two models.
cons: A server running very different models gets one number for all.

options.label: Per model too
cons: Rarely needed — most services report their own sizes.

steps.intro: Pulling in new models without waiting a day.

steps.path: The model menu in the chat, while searching
steps.headline: Besides the model picker's empty search, should Refresh model list appear anywhere else?
steps.today: The app re-downloads the model lists once a day. A model released this morning stays missing until then, and nothing can make it check sooner.
steps.problem: You search for a new model you know exists, get "No models match", and have no way forward.
steps.proposal: The empty search will offer Refresh model list. It could also live on the Cloud providers page.

options.label: Picker only
pros: It appears exactly when you notice something is missing.
No new button on the settings page.
cons: Hard to find if you aren't searching.

options.label: Picker and settings
cons: One more button on a page that's already busy.
